subtitle: How a Silent Assembly Gave Marathi a People’s Voice

panels.shot: nighttime wide shot of a village edge, torchlit figures gathering in secrecy under a banyan tree, with Chakradhara Swami in calm silhouette at the center
panels.action: Chakradhara Swami stands serene beneath a sprawling banyan at Ridhapur as villagers from many walks of life slip into the shadows around him, torches flickering against the dark plains of Vidarbha.

dialogue.text: In a quiet corner of the Yadava realm, Chakradhara Swami gathers a hidden crowd—and chooses Marathi over Sanskrit, leaving behind a people’s history the courts never wrote.

i18n.hi: यादव राज की एक शांत कोने में चक्रधर स्वामी गुप्त भीड़ जुटाते हैं — और संस्कृत छोड़ कर मराठी चुनते हैं, ऐसी लोककथा रचते हैं जो दरबारों ने नहीं लिखी।

panels.shot: broad aerial of the Deccan plateau, with Devagiri fort prominent, roads and towns dotting the landscape
panels.action: An expansive view of the Deccan shows the hill-fort of Devagiri rising above scattered towns and fields, caravan roads threading through a dry, sunlit plateau.

dialogue.text: Late thirteenth century. The Yadava kings of Devagiri rule from their hill-fort, while villages, traders, and farmers carry on their lives across the plateau.

i18n.hi: तेरहवीं सदी का उत्तरार्ध। देवगिरी के पहाड़ी किले से यादव राजा राज चलाते हैं, और पठार पर गाँव, व्यापारी, किसान अपनी-अपनी दुनिया में लगे हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Sanskrit school, brahmin teacher with palm-leaf manuscripts, students seated by caste rank
panels.action: Inside a shaded hall, a Brahmin teacher recites from a palm-leaf text as a few upper-caste students listen, seated in careful rows, while a barefoot boy peeks in from the doorway, excluded.

dialogue.text: Learning still speaks mainly in Sanskrit. Access is narrow, marked by caste and lineage, and most villagers meet sacred words as distant sounds, not their own speech.

i18n.hi: विद्या की ज़ुबान अभी भी ज़्यादातर संस्कृत है। रास्ता तंग है, जाति और वंश से बाँटा हुआ, और गाँववालों के लिए पवित्र शब्द बस दूर की ध्वनि हैं, अपनी बोली नहीं।

panels.shot: medium-low angle of Chakradhara Swami walking a dusty road with a small group trailing, simple robes, staff, bare feet
panels.action: Chakradhara Swami walks barefoot along a dusty village road, staff in hand, his face calm yet intense, as a few men and women of different dress and ornaments trail behind him, listening.

dialogue.text: Into this landscape walks Chakradhara Swami—a wandering teacher, later remembered as the second incarnation of Krishna, whose path will cut across caste and language lines.

i18n.hi: इसी धरती पर आते हैं चक्रधर स्वामी — घूमंतू गुरु, जिन्हें बाद में कृष्ण का दूसरा अवतार कहा जाएगा; जिनका रास्ता जाति और भाषा की दीवारें काटता चला जाएगा।

panels.shot: intimate village courtyard scene, Chakradhara seated on a low platform, mixed-caste villagers around, simple huts behind
panels.action: In a small courtyard, Chakradhara Swami sits on a low platform, speaking to a ring of men and women in varied clothing, from coarse farmer’s cloth to merchant’s fine cotton, all leaning in.

dialogue.text: In courtyards and by village wells, he speaks of devotion, discipline, and detachment, not in polished Sanskrit, but in the Marathi of daily life.

i18n.hi: आँगनों में, कुओं के पास, वे भक्ति, नियम और विराग की बातें करते हैं — चमकीली संस्कृत नहीं, रोज़ की बोलचाल वाली मराठी में।

panels.shot: close-up on Chakradhara’s face as he looks at two followers of different backgrounds sitting side by side
panels.action: Chakradhara Swami looks with quiet approval at a coarse-clothed labourer and a thread-wearing Brahmin sitting side by side, their earlier hesitation slowly easing.

dialogue.text: His Mahanubhava path draws workers, Brahmins, wandering mendicants, and householders to the same floor. For them, he lays down strict rules—and a startling equality.

i18n.hi: उनका महानुभाव मार्ग मज़दूरों, ब्राह्मणों, संन्यासियों और गृहस्थों को एक ही चौपाल पर बिठाता है। इन सबके लिए वे कड़े नियम रखते हैं — और हैरतभरी बराबरी भी।

panels.shot: evening wide shot of Ridhapur village outskirts, people converging quietly toward a banyan tree
panels.action: At dusk on the edge of Ridhapur, villagers move in ones and twos toward a large banyan tree, eyes alert, as the last light fades and the fields fall silent.

dialogue.text: Ridhapur in Vidarbha becomes one of his resting points. Here, followers gather quietly, some out of devotion, some out of curiosity, some despite their families’ anger.

i18n.hi: विदर्भ का रिधापूर उनका एक ठहराव बनता है। यहाँ शिष्य चुपचाप जुटते हैं — कोई भक्ति से, कोई जिज्ञासा से, कोई अपने घर की नाराज़गी की परवाह किए बिना।

panels.shot: medium shot under the banyan, Chakradhara seated, a few close disciples around, atmosphere of a council
panels.action: Under the banyan at Ridhapur, Chakradhara Swami sits cross-legged, surrounded by a small circle of close disciples, their faces tense with expectation, as the larger crowd waits a little further back.

dialogue.text: One gathering there will be remembered in their own texts as a decisive assembly, where they choose how their path will speak—and how it will survive.

i18n.hi: इन ही जमावड़ों में से एक को उनके ग्रंथों में निर्णायक सभा कहा जाएगा — जहाँ वे तय करेंगे कि उनका मार्ग किस ज़ुबान में बोलेगा, और कैसे बचा रहेगा।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of Chakradhara’s hand tapping the earth as he speaks, faces of disciples half-seen
panels.action: Chakradhara Swami’s hand rests firm on the bare earth as he leans slightly forward, disciples’ faces caught between firelight and shadow, straining to catch every word.

dialogue.text: Their discipline is exacting: rules for food, dress, travel, and speech. Now comes a new rule—about the very language that will carry their teachings.

i18n.hi: उनका अनुशासन सख़्त है: खाने, पहनने, सफ़र और बोलने के नियम अलग से। अब आता है नया नियम — उसी ज़ुबान को लेकर, जो उनकी शिक्षा ढोएगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chakradhara raising his hand slightly as if to forestall a suggestion, one disciple kneeling
panels.action: A kneeling disciple, head bowed, seems to have just spoken, while Chakradhara Swami lifts his hand gently, his gaze steady, as if turning aside a well-meant proposal.

dialogue.speaker: chakradhara_swami
dialogue.text: Let our path be spoken plainly, so all who hear may live it.

i18n.hi: "हमारा मार्ग सादा ज़ुबान में बोले, ताकि जो सुने, जी भी सके।"

panels.shot: wide shot of the assembly, with women and men of various dress reacting, some surprised, some relieved
panels.action: The gathered men and women exchange glances—some startled, some smiling in relief—as Chakradhara Swami’s words hang in the torchlit air at Ridhapur.

dialogue.text: Some may have expected Sanskrit for status, or a secret code for the few. Instead, the choice at Ridhapur affirms Marathi as their shared tongue.

i18n.hi: कुछ लोग शायद मान-सम्मान के लिए संस्कृत, या चंद लोगों के लिए गुप्त बोली की उम्मीद कर रहे थे। पर रिधापूर की इस सभा में मराठी को ही अपनी साझा ज़ुबान ठहराया जाता है।

panels.shot: quiet interior of a hut, a disciple reciting instructions in Marathi to another, both seated on the floor
panels.action: Inside a modest hut, a disciple with a simple cloth over his shoulder recites precise instructions in Marathi to another, who repeats them carefully, fingers counting each point.

dialogue.text: The Mahanubhavas will speak rules, stories, and praise in the words of farmers and traders, trusting that clear speech and firm practice can stand without Sanskrit ornament.

i18n.hi: महानुभाव अब नियम, कथा और स्तुति किसान और व्यापारी की बोली में कहेंगे — यक़ीन के साथ कि साफ़ शब्द और पक्का आचरण बिना संस्कृत साज-सज्जा के भी टिक सकते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mhaimbhat listening to an elder recounting episodes, palm-leaf and stylus beside him
panels.action: In another village courtyard, a thoughtful man sits with a palm-leaf and stylus beside him, listening intently as an older follower recounts episodes from Chakradhara’s life, gesturing for detail.

dialogue.text: Among those who hear and remember is Mhaimbhat, a Brahmin by birth, who will later compose the Lilacharitra, drawing on such spoken narratives.

i18n.hi: सुनने और याद रखने वालों में हैं म्हैमभट — जन्म से ब्राह्मण — जो आगे चलकर इन्हीं सुनी हुई कथाओं से लीळाचारित्र रचेंगे।

panels.shot: close-up of palm-leaf as Mhaimbhat’s hand inscribes Marathi prose, faint guide-lines visible
panels.action: A close view of a palm-leaf shows neat lines of Marathi words taking shape under Mhaimbhat’s steady hand, each letter etched with deliberate care.

dialogue.text: Between about 1278 and 1288, he writes their stories in Marathi prose—the earliest such prose we still have—careful, matter-of-fact, and rooted in the speech he heard.

i18n.hi: लगभग १२७८ से १२८८ के बीच वे उनकी कथाएँ मराठी गद्य में लिखते हैं — जो बचा हुआ सबसे प्राचीन गद्य है — सीधा, सूखा-सटीक, और सुनी हुई बोली में जड़ें जमाए।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of scenes described in Lilacharitra: markets, village disputes, pilgrim roads, all from ground level
panels.action: A broad montage shows a bustling market, a village dispute under a tree, and dusty pilgrims on the road to a shrine, all viewed at street level as ordinary people move through their days.

dialogue.text: In Lilacharitra, the Yadava realm appears not through royal deeds, but through grain prices, quarrels, pilgrim routes, and village gossip—details that the great courts rarely noticed.

i18n.hi: लीळाचारित्र में यादव राज्य राजाओं के कारनामों से नहीं, बल्कि अनाज के भाव, झगड़ों, तीर्थ-रास्तों और गाँव की चुगलियों से दिखता है — वो बारीकियाँ, जिन्हें बड़े दरबार अक्सर अनदेखा करते रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a traditional scholar in a later century reading the text, other manuscripts stacked nearby
panels.action: In a later, dimly lit room, a scholar bends over an old palm-leaf manuscript of Lilacharitra, other bundled leaves stacked around him, his lips silently shaping Marathi sentences.

dialogue.text: Centuries on, scholars will turn to this work for a rare, ground-level view of thirteenth-century Maharashtra, preserved because a sect committed to discipline also valued memory.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतने पर विद्वान इसी ग्रंथ की ओर लौटेंगे — तेरहवीं सदी के महाराष्ट्र की ज़मीन-स्तर की झाँकी के लिए, जो इसलिए बची कि एक अनुशासित पंथ ने स्मृति को भी धर्म माना।

panels.shot: close shot of a manuscript with unusual symbols and cipher-like characters, a careful hand tracing them
panels.action: A hand traces curious, compact symbols on an aged manuscript, the characters denser and more secretive than ordinary script, as if guarding their contents.

dialogue.text: Mahanubhava traditions also speak of ciphered manuscripts and strict rules of transmission, ways of protecting texts amid social suspicion and shifting powers.

i18n.hi: महानुभाव परम्पराएँ गुप्त लिपियों वाले पोथों और सख़्त परंपरा-वाचन की भी बात करती हैं — समाज की शंका और बदलती सत्ता के बीच ग्रंथों को बचाने की युक्तियाँ।

panels.shot: return to Ridhapur banyan scene, but now shown as a memory, Chakradhara calm as followers bow
panels.action: The banyan at Ridhapur appears again like a distant memory, Chakradhara Swami seated calmly as his mixed group of followers bow, their outlines fading at the edges.

dialogue.text: We do not hear of royal decrees against them in Ramachandra’s time, nor of court patronage. Their story moves instead through huts, roads, and such quiet assemblies.

i18n.hi: रामचंद्र के समय न तो उनके ख़िलाफ़ शाही फ़रमानों की चर्चा मिलती है, न दरबारी सरपरस्ती की; उनकी कथा तो झोपड़ियों, सड़कों और ऐसी ही शांत सभाओं के बीच बहती है।

panels.shot: final reflective wide shot of a modern Marathi-speaking town, people reading, teaching, chatting, subtle echo of the banyan in a roadside tree
panels.action: A present-day Marathi-speaking town bustles with readers, teachers, and shopkeepers, a large roadside tree casting shade over people talking as traffic moves around them.

dialogue.text: From that secret assembly at Ridhapur to the pages of Lilacharitra, the choice to think and write in Marathi helped make a people’s tongue into a language of memory and reflection.

i18n.hi: रिधापूर की उस गुप्त सभा से लेकर लीळाचारित्र के पन्नों तक, मराठी में सोचने-लिखने की इस चॉइस ने लोक-बोली को स्मृति और मनन की भाषा बनने का दम दिया।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Silent Assembly Gave Marathi a People’s Voice
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक मौन सभा ने मराठी को लोगों की आवाज़ कैसे दी
